headline: MaxMine deploying AI co-pilot for mining operations with 14 million hours of training data to enable real-time mine plan tracking
reasoning: Shaun Mitchell demonstrated MaxMine's AI co-pilot tool, which allows mining supervisors to query operational data in natural language and receive mobile-friendly reports within roughly 30 seconds. The system draws on approximately 14 million hours of proprietary mining data to provide contextual answers about equipment performance versus plan. In the demo, the tool surfaced excavator productivity data showing one unit running 18% ahead of plan, illustrating the practical utility for site supervisors. Mitchell positioned this as solving a real operational problem around real-time progress tracking against mine plans.
quote: So we've got some sort of canned prompts in there. So, um, if I was to sit there and the classic question the supervisor might ask is, are we on track to meet the targets? So that's the mine plan. And you'll see it going away here and picking up all the different parts of the reporting that we have underneath. We have about 14,000,000 hours worth of data we've been actually honing this AI on. So some of the best in the industry. And then what it will do is it's pulling that information in a really mobile friendly fashion, and then it will produce that for us. And there we go. Um, so about 30s. And so what it's telling me here is here's a snapshot of how you're going against planned. Um, we've got some excavators here, which is the X, and it's telling me that one's working on some waste and that it is actually 18% ahead of plan.
episode_title: Mining industry gets new AI co-pilot
